'''Thomas Zink''' (born 14 April 1949 in [[Berlin]]) is a German mathematician. He currently holds a chair for [[Arithmetics|arithmetic]] [[algebraic geometry]] at [[Bielefeld University]]. 
He has been doing research at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]], at the [[University of Toronto]] and at the [[University of Bonn]] among others.

In 1992, he was awarded the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]] joint with [[Christopher Deninger]] ([[Westfälische Wilhelms-Universität]] of [[Münster (Westfalen)|Münster]]), [[Michael Rapoport]] ([[University of Wuppertal]]) and [[Peter Schneider (mathematician)|Peter Schneider]] ([[University of Cologne]]). The four researchers succeeded to apply modern methods of algebraic geometry to the solution of [[diophantine equation]]s. 
Furthermore, he is a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] ([[Halle an der Saale]]).
